ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a shunt zener regulator circuit: on the left side is a Vsource = 24 V power supply, above the power supply is a series-connected resistor labeled 1.2 kΩ, the output node after the series resistor is connected downward through a zener diode to ground, beside the diode is labeled Vz = 7.9 V; on the right side of the same output node there is also a load resistor Rload connected in parallel to ground. Reasoning: The problem gives Rload = 1.5 kΩ. When the zener diode conducts and regulates voltage, the output node voltage is clamped at 7.9 V. The series resistor current is Is = (24 - 7.9) / 1.2 kΩ = 16.1 / 1.2 kΩ = 13.4167 mA. The load current is IL = 7.9 / 1.5 kΩ = 5.2667 mA. By the node current law, the zener diode current Izener = Is - IL = 13.4167 - 5.2667 = 8.15 mA.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a shunt zener regulator: 24 V source, 1.2 kΩ series resistor, zener clamp Vz = 7.9 V, and Rload to ground. From the text take Rload = 1.5 kΩ. Since the zener clamps the output node to 7.9 V, compute the series current Is = (24 - 7.9)/1.2 kΩ. Compute the load current IL = 7.9/1.5 kΩ. Then use KCL, Izener = Is - IL, giving about 8.15 mA.

method.method_draft: First identify the image circuit values: Vs = 24 V, Rs = 1.2 kΩ, zener clamp Vz = 7.9 V, with load in parallel with the zener. From the text use Rload = 1.5 kΩ. Transform the 24 V source and 1.2 kΩ series resistor into a Norton source: IN = 24/1.2 kΩ = 20 mA in parallel with 1.2 kΩ. With the zener regulating, the node is at 7.9 V, so current through the Norton resistor is 7.9/1.2 kΩ and load current is 7.9/1.5 kΩ. The zener current is IN minus those two currents, which evaluates to about 8.15 mA.
